svg.title: An internal exchange lifts from a nonzero fixed corner
svg.desc: For a factor R with involution beta, a nonzero beta-fixed corner detects innerness. Orthogonal range projections of partial isometries and their beta images construct the unique global lift. In the semifinite case an inner symmetry has a finite fixed corner, but this does not make either compressed copy multiplicative or establish the stable ambient isomorphism.
svg.text: A full corner detects inner exchange
Proposition 5I.5 · Corollary 5I.6
The actual factor and its corner
R a factor, β² = id, 0 ≠ e = β(e)
eRe is a factor; its central support is 1.
βₑ is an automorphism of this same corner.
The centre test supplies a corner symmetry
C(βₑ) not a factor ⇔ βₑ = Ad t
t ∈ eRe, t = t*, t² = e
Use the two-by-two algebra of (5I.1).
Cover the factor by range projections
v₀ = e, pᵢ = vᵢ*vᵢ ≤ e, qᵢ = vᵢvᵢ*
qᵢqⱼ = 0 (i ≠ j), Σ qᵢ = 1
Maximality uses fRe ≠ 0 for nonzero f.
The pᵢ may overlap; the qᵢ are orthogonal.
Two orthogonal partitions give a unitary
wᵢ = β(vᵢ)t vᵢ*, u = Σ wᵢ ∈ R
wᵢ*wᵢ = qᵢ, wᵢwᵢ* = β(qᵢ)
Both sums are 1; u and u* converge strongly.
All sums use finite subsets of the index set.
The corner equation lifts every coefficient
bᵢⱼ = vᵢ*a vⱼ ∈ eRe, β(bᵢⱼ)t = tbᵢⱼ
β(a)u = ua, ue = t, u² = 1
Thus u = u* implements β inside R.
The prescribed corner value makes u unique.
Semifinite trace: an existential finite test
An inner symmetry has a nonzero eigenspace.
A finite-trace spectral cut inside it gives e.
0 < T(e) < ∞, β(e) = e, C(βₑ) nonfactor
The whole source problem retains its clauses
A fixed e need not commute with A or B.
Compression defects may still have norm 1.
Both full commutants and the actual onto Θ
remain required by Theorem 5I.3.
